note: Digging by hand (sprint 124: the shovel, .agents/planning/sprint-124-shovel.md): what moves loose ground. A tool works the world in its own cells (`cell`, sixteenths). `shape: bore`: a ring `across` wide is cast onto what they look at, the next few cells lit, and held, it takes the tool's cells along their look, out to `along`, the nearest still there first, one at a time, `rate` a second, the next few lit: what's between them and the face, then the face chip by chip, so held it opens a round hole they can walk into. `shape: cell` is the cell of the tool's grid (`along`, every way) aimed into, outlined, and held, each swing digs one, a sweep digging what it passes. A form's box is outlined whole where it's aimed, and held, each swing takes `bite` sixteenths of it, the highest first, till it's gone. `tools`: each digging tool's item definition (as hand.json's), the groups of blocks it moves, and its `bite`. `operations`: the forms F offers with one held, each in sizes (sixteenths: `along` the way they face, `across` it, `deep` down), the first what's done before any's chosen. Its `shape`: `cell`, as above; `box`, the whole box under the ground's top where aimed; `round`, a pit, the round the box bounds; `level`, everything over a level (their feet; Shift: the ground aimed at) up to `deep` above it. None adds ground. `scoop`: what the inventory holds dug ground as, one item for every soil (which, in its metadata), each 16 × 16 × 4 sixteenths of it, four to a block.
